thread.title: Apple Well Positioned For Resurgence - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)

author: Erich Reimer
title: Apple Well Positioned For Resurgence - Apple Inc. (NASDAQ:AAPL)
text:
Apple's ( AAPL ) recent price collapse, amid a general downturn in the markets, seemingly makes it an excellent value proposition at the moment due to the current expected trajectory of continued growth the company has. Even amid some weakness in guidance and market worries, the company is not likely to fall further due to the sheer amount of revenue and earnings it seems positioned to continue pulling in and its historical behavior amid market troubles.
Based on that, at this price point I believe Apple's risk-reward leans heavily on the side of low expected downside but high potential for resurgence.
Apple Has Collapsed With The Markets But Continues To Rake In Earnings And Growth On Nov. 1, 2018, Apple reported its Q4 2018 earnings . The earnings report itself was quite positive , as the company beat expectations on earnings, revenue, and average iPhone sales price, but missed expectations on iPhone sales. The combination of no longer reporting detailed iPhone, Mac, and iPad sales figures combined with slightly decelerated guidance has sent the stock tumbling over 34% since then, far more than the general equity markets as a whole. At $146 a share the stock is now down over 35% from its $232 a share high in early October and at levels not seen since 2017.
AAPL data by YCharts However I believe that the light guidance and reporting change cannot possibly justify the company's decline of over 33% in response, particularly as the company's revenue and earnings are expected to continue to generally increase. Indeed, as shown below, Apple's TTM PE ratio and forward PE ratio are now at lows not seen since the general market stagnation of 2016.
AAPL PE Ratio (TTM) data by YCharts Given that Apple's own earnings trajectory justifies not only rallying back to its former price levels seen just a few months ago but even beyond that, I believe the biggest factor holding Apple back right now is the general uncertain and negative mood in domestic equity markets. However even despite that, as long as the market doesn't collapse completely, I believe Apple is extremely well positioned to rally up at least moderately in the short term and undoubtedly much more in the long term.
The fact is that Apple, as I've explained before , is a company that's rapidly diversifying and each quarter is showing that it's continuing to do so. As shown below the company is continuing to see the extraordinary double-digit growth in "services" and "other" (which, according to the Q4 2018 earnings call, will soon be "wearables, home, and accessories") that's allowing the company to create new growth opportunities for itself through mechanisms such as the highly successful App Store . The company continues too to see vibrant growth too across nearly all regions.
(Source: Apple Q4 2018 Earnings Data Summary )
The company is guiding for between $89 billion and $93 billion in revenue in Q1 2019, which admittedly is unfortunately between roughly flat year-on-year and at most 5% growth compared to Q1 2018 . Either way it still will be a record quarter even if not at the double-digit revenue growth numbers Apple often posts.
The expected 38% to 38.5% gross margin is holding steady, but undoubtedly there are significant worries over whether both the current tariffs conflict with China and general market headwinds are going to old back Apple growth.
Yet even with this picture and all the real risks Apple faces I believe that the company still is now in oversold territory even if its growth is currently facing some turbulence. The company, simply put, is and will continue to bring in earnings that do not justify the extraordinarily low valuation multiple it now faces. Therefore the change in price is not due to belief in a decline in Apple earnings themselves but rather in the originally priced-in growth, creating a P/E reduction to now these incredibly low levels.
Apple's history has shown its P/E ratio can continue to dip even slightly further to a 9-10 range but that would likely be the lowest it could possibly go. Rather, if markets stabilize and Apple continues to post growth, beating expectations that it may have a flat upcoming Q1 2019, then the company is very likely to experience a significant rebound. If markets as a whole begin moving up again then the pessimistic attitude currently holding down the company likely will fade and accelerate the upturn again too.
Conclusion As I've explained many times over the course of this year I believe Apple is a company that, even at its behemoth size (although reduced significantly in the past few months), is showing ample ability to grow through geographic diversification, finding new ways to innovate the iPhone and increase average sales price without sacrificing units sold, and expanding rapidly into a wide array of accessories and services.
All of these factors are only shown to be continuing in Q4 2018's earnings report. Q1 2019 guidance, and general market worries, are real cause for concern. However, as I've explained, Apple's further downside even amid more market weakness may be limited due to historical P/E ratios and even a relatively weak Q1 2019 still justifies a far higher price than Apple's current valuation. If anything shows a positive surprise for Apple or the wider markets then the company could experience even greater a resurgence.
For these reasons I believe Apple at this point is extremely attractive on a risk-reward proposition. The risks are there but seem to have mostly exhausted themselves while the possibility of a well-justified rally are enormous.
Disclosure: I/we have no positions in any stocks mentioned, and no plans to initiate any positions within the next 72 hours.
